sites.tag_type: N-TAP (protein G + SBP); also ALFA, BC2, 6E
sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Antagonist binding (radioligand): Kd indistinguishable from WT (L3). Agonist-induced cAMP accumulation: N-terminally tagged receptor behaves like untagged (no rightward shift), as stated explicitly in L4's comparison group.
sites.rationale: A2AR has no signal peptide; the topology landmarks place residues 1–7 as extracellular, making insert_after_residue=0 (prepend before Met1) the sole unambiguous N-terminal extracellular junction. Both PMC3789979 (L3/L5) and PMC12633870 (L6/L7/L8) independently report full-length, membrane-anchored A2AR constructs carrying tags at this N-terminus, confirming the position is tolerated. L3 provides the strongest functional evidence: antagonist binding is WT-equivalent, and L4's explicit comparison group shows N-terminal-tagged cAMP response is indistinguishable from untagged. The 7-residue extracellular N-terminal span (MPIMGSS) provides adequate distance (≥3 aa) from TM1 (residue 8) for a short epitope tag. PMC3789979 (L3/L5): N-terminally TAP-tagged full-length A2AR stably expressed in HEK293 cells; antagonist radioligand binding affinity indistinguishable from WT. L4 (same paper) reports that agonist-induced cAMP accumulation was shifted 20-fold in the C-terminally tagged construct 'compared with N-terminally tagged and untagged receptors', explicitly placing the N-terminal construct on par with untagged. PMC12633870 (L6/L7/L8) independently engrafted ALFA, BC2, and 6E epitope tags into the 'distal N-terminus (extracellular portion)' of full-length A2AR for nanobody-based detection. Neither paper names a specific junction residue; A2AR has no signal peptide, so the extracellular N-terminus begins at Met1 and the only unambiguous prepend position is insert_after_residue=0.

sources.claim: Accordingly, we examined several constructs (see schematic representation in Fig. 1 A ); when stably expressed in HEK293 cells, both N- and C-terminally tagged constructs gave rise to receptors that bound the antagonist with an affinity indistinguishable from the wild type A 2A receptor ( Fig. 1 B ).

literature_notes: Only one extracellular surface site is supported by the ledger: the N-terminal prepend (insert_after_residue=0). L3/L5 (PMC3789979) and L6/L7/L8 (PMC12633870) both pin the same junction (N-terminal prepend), so they constitute one site; L3 is cited as primary for its functional data. ECL1 (69–74), ECL2 (145–171), and ECL3 (260–264) are extracellular loops but no ledger line reports a tolerated tag insertion in any of them for A2AR or a close ortholog — no site is proposed for those loops. The C-terminal tag (L1/L2, L4) is intracellular (residues 289–412) and shows perturbed agonist signaling; it is recorded in other_positions. ICL3 insertions (L9, L10) are intracellular and recorded in other_positions.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal tag (3xHA-2xMyc CRISPR knock-in, L1/L2; TAP tag, L3/L4) is intracellular (residues 289–412); agonist-induced cAMP accumulation shifted ~20-fold rightward vs N-terminally tagged and untagged receptors (L4), indicating impaired G-protein coupling despite normal surface expression and antagonist binding.
